_about: Planner assumptions (guide section 7.3). Every value has a source; values marked 'derived' are our own arithmetic on a cited figure. All values are editable on the website. Compiled 27 Oct 2026.

howToRead.cost: Cost to the programme per household reached, in RWF (one-off; fuel not included).
howToRead.usage: Share of households that actually use the new stove as their main stove (sustained use).
howToRead.effect: Share of a child's smoke-related risk of cough with fast breathing removed when the stove is used. Given as a range: 'trial' = randomised-trial point estimate; 'observational' = upper bound derived from observational studies.
howToRead.rankingNote: Cost, usage and effect are the same in every district, so they change the totals but not which districts come first.

effectEvidence.summary: Randomised trials, including HAPIN which had a site in Rwanda (Kayonza), did not show a statistically significant reduction in severe infant pneumonia from LPG cooking (IRR 0.96, 98.75% CI 0.64-1.44). Observational studies associate solid-fuel use with higher child pneumonia risk (pooled OR 1.78). Our own Rwanda survey model also finds no significant fuel effect after adjustment. Cases averted are therefore shown as a range of scenarios, not a prediction.

sources.finding: LPG intervention: severe pneumonia 5.67 vs 6.06 per 100 child-years, IRR 0.96 (98.75% CI 0.64-1.44); child PM2.5 24.2 vs 66.0 ug/m3
sources.citation: McCollum ED et al. (HAPIN Investigators). N Engl J Med 2024;390:32-43

sources.finding: Unprocessed solid fuel use and pneumonia in children under 5: pooled OR 1.78 (95% CI 1.45-2.18)
sources.citation: Dherani M et al. Bull World Health Organ 2008;86(5):390-398

sources.finding: Chimney woodstove: physician-diagnosed pneumonia RR 0.84 (0.63-1.13); severe pneumonia reduced by about a third
Advanced-combustion biomass stoves cut kitchen PM2.5 by 41% (29-50%) and personal exposure by 55% (19-87%); levels stay above WHO guidelines
sources.citation: Pope D et al. Environment International 2017;101:7-18

stoves.name: LPG gas stove kit
stoves.costSource: Stove price 'as much as' Rwf 150,000 (2-burner stove + 12 kg cylinder + pay-as-you-go valve kit programme). KT Press, Oct 2025: https://www.ktpress.rw/2025/10/50000-households-to-get-free-cooking-gas-kits-courtesy-of-rwanda-saudi-deal/ . Refill Rwf 22,000-28,000 per 12 kg (about 2 months), not included: New Times 2026 https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/35066/news/energy/why-gas-retailers-are-charging-different-prices-across-rwanda
stoves.usageSource: HAPIN trial: biomass stove used on a median 0.4% of monitored days, but with free LPG and close monitoring. Real-world use is likely lower; no Rwanda field data found. Lower this value to test refill-cost risk.
stoves.effectSource: trial = 1 - IRR 0.96 (HAPIN, not significant); observational = 1 - 1/1.78 (derived from Dherani 2008 pooled OR, assumes exposure fully removed)

stoves.name: Improved biomass cookstove (Tier 3)
stoves.costSource: EAQIP clean-cooking results-based financing: worked example of a Tier 3 stove priced Rwf 45,000 with a Rwf 36,000 subsidy (household pays 9,000). Current rule: Tier 3 subsidy 80%, cap Rwf 38,000. BRD, EAQIP Component 3b Clean Cooking RBF Operations Manual Ver 05 (1 Mar 2024), section 6.7 and Table 2: https://www.brd.rw/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/EAQIP_CC-RBF_OM_-_Ver_0306-04-2022.pdf . Use 45,000 for full price without subsidy.
stoves.usageSource: Rwanda, free EcoZoom stoves to ~100k households: 83.3% of households observed cooking were using it at about 1 year (51.3% also used other stoves). Barstow CK et al. BMC Public Health 2016;16:584 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4947312 . Pilot exclusive use was only 28.5% at 5 months (Barstow et al. PLoS One 2014).
stoves.effectSource: trial = 1 - RR 0.84 (RESPIRE chimney stove, not significant); observational = 0.44 x 0.48 (derived: Dherani upper bound scaled by the ~41-55% exposure reduction in Pope 2017)

stoves.name: Electric pressure cooker
stoves.costSource: List price Rwf 85,000 (pilot discounted to Rwf 40,000), electricity not included. SEforALL 2023, Examining the Experience of Using EPCs in Urban Households in Kigali: https://www.seforall.org/system/files/2023-11/report-rwanda-clean-cooking-final.pdf
stoves.usageSource: Kigali pilot (n=100, ~3 months): EPC used in 41% of cooking events; charcoal meals fell from 67% to 45%. Same SEforALL 2023 report. Longer follow-up not found.
stoves.effectSource: Clean fuel, same evidence as LPG (no EPC-specific health trial found). Applies only to meals cooked on the EPC, which the usage rate captures.
